findings.evidence: Bodies at 362-369, 387-390, 406-413 are character-identical modulo `hx` vs `hx.ne'`; `grep -rn "xBj_ne_zero\|ne_zero_of_xBj" code/` finds no existing such lemma, and `Kinematics/Basic.lean:56` is the only place `xBj` is defined.
findings.fix: Extract `lemma pq_ne_zero_of_xBj_ne_zero (g) (K) (hx : K.xBj g ≠ 0) : g K.p K.q ≠ 0` and `lemma q_sq_ne_zero_of_xBj_ne_zero ... : g K.q K.q ≠ 0` (they depend only on `xBj = Q2 / (2 p·q)` and `Q2 = -q²`), and call them in all five places.
findings.issue: The same four-line proof of `hpq : g K.p K.q ≠ 0` from `hx` is repeated at lines 362-365, 387-390 and 406-409, and the parallel `hQ2 : g K.q K.q ≠ 0` proof at lines 366-369 and 410-413. Repeated reasoning that is a reusable kinematic fact, not a one-off.

findings.evidence: `Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Ring/Unbundled/Basic.lean:362`: `theorem mul_nonneg_iff_of_pos_left (h : 0 < c) : 0 ≤ c * b ↔ 0 ≤ b`; `hT` determines `c` but leaves `b` a metavariable.
findings.fix: Pin the argument: `rw [← mul_nonneg_iff_of_pos_left (b := FLExact M (K.xBj g) (K.Q2 g) F1 (structureF2 g K F2c)) hT, ← key, mul_nonneg_iff_of_pos_left (show (0:ℝ) < 2 * K.xBj g by positivity)]`.
findings.issue: `rw [← mul_nonneg_iff_of_pos_left hT, ...]` rewrites with a RHS of the shape `0 ≤ ?b`, so which side of the iff is multiplied by `p_T · p_T` is fixed only by rw's first match; nothing in the script says the intended target is `0 ≤ FLExact ...`.

findings.evidence: Lines 414-417: `h1` is `Q2_mul_pTransverse_self` after `rw [hTwist, mul_zero, zero_add]`, i.e. `K.Q2 g * g p_T p_T = g K.p K.q ^ 2`.
findings.fix: Write it explicitly: `have h2 : K.Q2 g * g (pTransverse g K) (pTransverse g K) ≠ 0 := by rw [h1]; exact pow_ne_zero 2 hpq` then `exact right_ne_zero_of_mul h2`.
findings.issue: `exact right_ne_zero_of_mul (h1 ▸ pow_ne_zero 2 hpq)` relies on the elaborator inferring the `▸` motive backwards from the expected type `?a * ?b ≠ 0`; the reader cannot see that `h1 : K.Q2 g * g p_T p_T = (p·q)^2` is being used right-to-left.

summary: The new proofs are short and mostly robust, but the derivation of `g p q ≠ 0` (and `g q q ≠ 0`) from `xBj ≠ 0` is copy-pasted across three theorems instead of being a lemma, and two one-liners (a wildcard `rw ←` and a `▸` motive) hide why they work.
